title: Is Russia planning to attack a Nato country? | BBC News
summary: A BBC News explainer on whether Russia plans to attack a NATO country, covering a European sabotage wave, drone incursions near Poland and warnings from Tusk, Macron and Rutte.

assertions.quote: Russia is testing our limit. They're probing almost every day now.
the Trump administration has been pretty soft in signaling about its support for this Article 5 defense for for Europe
this is probably the most serious situation in in Western Moscow relations or the Kremlin

verdicts.note: Threat assessments, the Doomsday Clock and forecasters agree that Russia-West risk is higher than at any point since 1991, though still unlikely in any year.

Kroenig says the world was safest in the 1990s and 2000s and the indicators began to decline in the 2010s and 2020s, and respondents fear a risk of major-power war; it is an expert view, not a measured risk.

The Bulletin's record-close Clock setting cites increasingly aggressive great powers and a winner-takes-all competition, but the Clock is a composite of nuclear, climate, biological and AI risk, not a measure of great-power war alone.
CFR's expert survey says the risk of great-power war 'persists' and rates Taiwan and Russia-NATO contingencies at even odds for 2026, but makes no comparison with earlier decades.

UCDP: interstate conflicts doubled two years running to 8 in 2025, the most since WWII, and the authors say this lends credence to claims that Pax Americana is ending; none of these conflicts is between great powers.

UCDP's analyst says the recent rise in interstate conflicts indicates increased international tension and a changing global security order; this counts conflicts and does not estimate great-power war risk.

PRIO: eight international conflicts in 2025, the most since 1946, reflecting growing global tension and a Middle East escalation that continued into a USA-Iran war in 2026; none is a direct great-power war.

The WEF report says conflict-risk indicators are at their worst since the Second World War and that close to two-thirds of 1,300 experts see the two-year geopolitical outlook as turbulent or stormy. Its measures cover state-based conflict generally, not great-power war, and the survey ranks state-based armed conflict below geoeconomic confrontation.

assertions.quote: There is a real risk that drones or other types of projectiles will enter the territory of one or several countries on the eastern flank

verdicts.note: Russian drones repeatedly entered Polish, Romanian and Baltic airspace in 2025, with Moscow denying intent.
DDIS reports Russian drones and jets repeatedly violating NATO airspace, sharply more in 2025, and calls the mass drone incursion into Poland a likely deliberate provocation rather than an accident.
Eurasia Group expects Russian airspace probes and more frequent dangerous confrontations with NATO in 2026, but does not predict strikes on NATO territory passed off as accidents.

assertions.quote: to convince NATO member states, as we have already seen happen, that Article 5 is more theoretical than practical.

verdicts.note: This is a claim about the Kremlin's intent; the probing fits it but cannot show it.
DDIS assesses Russia's hybrid attacks aim to undermine NATO cohesion and that provocations could test whether the US would actually come to Europe's aid.

assertions.quote: I don't think Vladimir Putin is suicidal. So, I don't think he's about to launch a missile directly into the heart of Warsaw.
